projectTitle: asc — Apple App Store Connect CLI
description: A non-interactive CLI for the Apple App Store Connect API. Covers apps, versions, builds, TestFlight, in-app purchases and subscriptions, pricing, territory availability, screenshots and video assets, age ratings and App Store submission, plus a raw `asc api` escape hatch for the full JSON:API surface. Authenticates with an App Store Connect API key (issuer id, key id, .p8) and generates a fresh ES256 JWT per invocation. Built for scripts and AI agents: nothing prompts, and the complete reference is embedded in the binary behind `asc llm`.
rules: Authentication needs an App Store Connect API key with a management role: issuer id (UUID), key id (10 chars) and the .p8 private key, registered with `asc configure` or supplied via ASC_ISSUER_ID plus ASC_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH or ASC_PRIVATE_KEY_BASE64. App Store Server API (In-App Purchase) keys from the same issuer return 401 against the management API — they are different keys.
The .p8 private key cannot be re-downloaded from Apple. Never print its contents, never pass it inline on a command line, and never move or delete the user's copy.

Asset uploads validate asynchronously. A 2xx on reserve/PUT/commit does NOT mean acceptance — failures such as IMAGE_INCORRECT_DIMENSIONS surface later in assetDeliveryState. Check the final state before reporting success.

IAP and subscription review screenshots accept only legacy sizes (1242x2208, 2208x1242, 2048x2732, 2732x2048). Current App Store screenshot sizes are rejected: the appScreenshots validator and the review-screenshot validator are different. `asc iap screenshot` offers --auto-fit to resize and pad.

App availability requires ALL territories explicitly — roughly 175 territoryAvailabilities in a single POST, each with available true or false. `Japan only` still needs every other territory marked false. `asc availability set` expands the list automatically.

Free apps still need a price schedule (a customerPrice 0 price point) via `asc pricing set --free`. Price and availability are required for submission but stay unset even when the version page looks complete.
whatsNew is not editable on an app's first version and returns 409. IAPs created for sandbox testing often already exist, so POST 409s on a duplicate productId — `asc iap create` is find-or-create.

Inline-created (`included`) resources need local ids in the form ${name}. A plain string id returns 409 ENTITY_ERROR.INCLUDED.INVALID_ID. This matters when composing raw `asc api` POSTs for appPriceSchedules, appAvailabilities or offer codes.

`asc api` follows JSON:API: paginate with a limit query parameter (max 200) and follow links.next until absent; quote the path in shells because filter[...] contains brackets. Prefer a dedicated asc command when one exists — those already handle the traps above.

Some things have no public API and cannot be automated: the App Privacy questionnaire (/v1/apps/{id}/dataUsages 404s), App Store Server Notifications URL configuration, and Japan's 特定商取引法 disclosure. Direct the user to the web UI instead of retrying.

The complete reference is embedded in the binary: `asc llm` (Markdown) or `asc llm --format json`. It is regenerated from the cobra command tree, so prefer it over any remembered command list. Use --dry-run before any mutating command.
